about: Expected scope-fingerprint bytes for the consumer contract this repository's
reference provider adapts to. Each digest was produced by executing the consumer's
own inventory_scope_fingerprint over the named inputs, not by re-deriving the recipe
here -- a fixture written from a second reading of the spec agrees with the spec and
not necessarily with the code, which is the failure this file exists to prevent.
The recipe: exactly three components, as sorted [name, value] string pairs, in
compact UTF-8 JSON, SHA-256. hidden_allowlist is itself compact canonical JSON of the
sorted names. ensure_ascii is false throughout, which is why a non-ASCII name is one
of the cases: with it true the payload is byte-different and every digest below is
wrong while every same-implementation test still passes.
Not components: symlink traversal, filesystem boundaries, walk order, watch mode, and
special-object admission. Those are either fixed consumer semantics or provider
policy, and an adapter that hashed one would produce an identity the consumer cannot
reproduce. The adapter holds them as constants and refuses options that disagree,
which is checked rather than hashed.

cases.name: consumer-defaults
cases.why: the config a consumer gets without asking for anything

cases.name: this-repository-s-provider
cases.why: the scope open_tree actually opens, so the digest and the open cannot drift

cases.name: provider-allowlist
cases.why: a two-name allowlist, so the order case below has two names to reorder; the provider's own scope is the next case

cases.name: allowlist-order-is-not-identity
cases.why: the allowlist is a set, so its written order must not reach the digest

cases.name: empty-allowlist
cases.why: an empty structured value still encodes, as [] rather than as absent

cases.name: non-ascii-allowlist
cases.why: the case that catches ensure_ascii, and the only one that can

cases.name: narrow-scope
cases.why: the smallest legal bounds, so a digest cannot be reading a default
